integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Expressive stylized 3D cartoon animation of an energetic peaceful Brazilian gamers protest, warm afternoon light, rounded original adult characters, matte colorful clothes, coherent five-finger hands. Vertical 768x1344 composition, one continuous wide-medium camera shot throughout. The reporter is an adult medium-brown woman with a short rounded curly dark afro, yellow blazer, white shirt and blue jeans. The interviewee beside her has tan skin, short swept dark hair, rectangular black glasses, short stubble, plain teal T-shirt and dark jeans. Reporter left, man right. Their faces are large, naturally expressive and always visible. The microphone is entirely plain black, without stickers or symbols. Same grounded comic street-report tone.
Exactly TWO large protest placards exist in this shot. Both are rectangular warm-ivory BLANK cardboard boards, with a simple thick dark navy rectangular outer border and a perfectly clean unmarked interior. Their entire surface remains visible above all heads: left board in the upper-left corner, right board in the upper-right corner, both occupy about one third of image width and the upper quarter of its height. Two background adults hold the boards upright above their heads on wooden stakes, facing the camera. Keep these boards nearly frontoparallel, separated from each other, without fingers, hair, flags or any object crossing their faces. Their interiors remain completely unmarked plain paper for the entire take. Other protesters have empty hands and raised fists only. The background is a simple warm brick facade, windows and trees with unmarked surfaces. Clothing is plain except for one small controller pictogram on the teal shirt. There is no visible lettering on any object or surface in the raw animation; the placard typography is added by the editor later.
0-4.0s: The crowd lifts the two blank boards and chants to the supplied Brazilian Portuguese audio. A slow economical physical dolly right reveals foreground stick parallax without changing shot size or cutting. Reporter and man wait amid the protest, with one spontaneous glance toward the crowd.
4.0-7.0s: The reporter turns to the man and asks exactly the question heard in the supplied audio, with matching mouth timing. She extends the plain microphone naturally, and he listens without mouthing her words.
7.0-9.1s: He glances down at his one set of real car keys, takes a small breath, and prepares to answer. Reporter holds the microphone near him.
9.1-12.8s: The man speaks in sync with the supplied audio, exactly <d>[Portuguese] Pra comprar uma placa de vídeo, eu tenho que vender o carro!</d>. He raises that single set of car keys in his right hand on the punchline; his left hand remains open and empty. Reporter watches him and then the keys.
12.8-15.083s: Reporter reacts with a single surprised glance, the crowd responds with an amused cheer and one forward step. The two blank boards sway gently above the heads, still fully visible and facing the lens. Ongoing bodily action through the last frame. The man still holds just one set of keys in one hand. All original audio, timing and voices come from the supplied soundtrack, which remains unchanged.
overall_soundscape: Use only the supplied original native Brazilian Portuguese interview soundtrack at its exact original timing and speed. Preserve voices, crowd and ambience; add no new words, voices, music or effects.
